title: POC scoping: cost modeling & benchmarks - Elysium Health
summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, workload sizing, and benchmark plan for a 6-week POC. Main focus: per-token cost estimates, batching/caching knobs, and budget constraints. Action items: share cost model, run benchmark harness, and confirm infra/KMS requirements.
action_items: Grace Li: Send initial cost model spreadsheet and sample Redwood config by 2025-12-05
Diego Ramos: Prep benchmark plan and test harness, target run week of 2025-12-08
Maya Patel: Provide production prompt set, average sequence lengths and expected qps by 2025-12-06
Ethan Zhou: Confirm network/VPC constraints, KMS provider and audit log requirements by 2025-12-10
next_steps: Redwood to send cost model and recommended batching/caching knobs
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and prompt set
Schedule benchmark run and agree on metrics/SLAs
Follow up meeting to review benchmark results and pricing proposal
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-03 15:00 PST — Duration: 58m
Attendees: Grace Li, Diego Ramos (Redwood); Maya Patel, Ethan Zhou, Sara Kim (Elysium Health)

[00:00] Grace: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick intro — Grace from Redwood AE, and Diego our systems SE. We're here to scope the POC for cost modeling and benchmarks. Maya you wanna kick off with goals?
[00:17] Maya: Yeah thanks Grace. Main thing for us is to validate the unit economics for a gen-ai assistant in our health app. So throughput targets around 200 qps at peak, avg prompt 120 tokens, response ~220 tokens. Need to understand per-token cost and how batching / cache will change that. Also timeline — we want a 6 week POC ideally.
[00:35] Diego: Awesome. Couple clarifying q's: when you say 200 qps is that concurrent user requests or end-to-end api calls? Also are you expecting streaming?
[00:44] Maya: 200 api calls per second at peak, mostly non-streaming now but we'd like streaming as an option later. Latency SLO for P0 is p95 < 450ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), and p95 < 900ms for longer. Cost target is under $0.003 per generated token across avg workloads — ballpark.
[01:05] Grace: Good, that's helpful. For cost we usually provide a baseline per-token estimate for hosted and then delta for dedicated; we model batching and KV/prefix cache impacts. We should also get a sample prompt distribution so we can model batching efficiency.
[01:22] Ethan: On infra side we have a VPC and strict egress rules, KMS is AWS KMS. We'll need private deployment options or dedicated capacity with VPC peering.
[01:31] Diego: That's fine. For the POC we can run either on Redwood hosted with a private VPC peering or Dedicated nodes in your account. The main cost differences are reserved GPU commit vs hosted per-token pricing. Also note batching efficiency depends heavily on qps shape — spiky traffic reduces batching savings.
[01:55] Sara: Can you explain the KV cache thing — we heard Redwood has a KV cache that reduces cost?
[02:02] Diego: Yeah KV cache — sorry sometimes transcriptions write K-V cache — it's our prefix caching. If you have repeated context or conversational sessions, we can reuse the KV cache to avoid recomputing early layers which saves token compute. That reduces per-token cost, especially for assistant with multi-turn. We estimate 10-40% savings depending on reuse.
[02:22] Maya: Great. For success criteria we want: 1) cost under $X/token (we'll give target after we share prompt set), 2) latency SLOs met at p95, 3) quality equivalent to current model (we'll provide eval prompts), and 4) deployment security requirements met (SOC2, KMS, audit logs).
[02:44] Grace: Makes sense. On quality we'll run our eval harness — Diego can run side-by-side runs to measure token/perf tradeoffs and regression. Typical knobs: model variant selection, quantization, batching window, and cache hit strategy.
[03:05] Diego: For benchmarking plan I propose: a) ingest sample prompt set + traffic profile, b) run three variants — hosted large public model, quantized dedicated variant, and hosted with prefix cache enabled — measure latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. c) we capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, and cost.
[03:28] Ethan: How do you compute cost per token — is it GPU time converted to $ or a flat price?
[03:33] Grace: We model it from GPU-second cost plus infra overhead and share per-token and per-inference estimates. For hosted we show an all-in per-token number; for dedicated we show the math: monthly commit cost divided by tokens served at expected utilization plus ops overhead. We'll send the spreadsheet so you can modify assumptions.
[03:53] Sara: Any examples of numbers? Even roughs?
[03:56] Grace: Roughly, on a highly batched scenario per-token can be under $0.0015 for some open Llama variants when quantized and well-batched. For low-latency single-stream calls you might see $0.0025-0.004. Those are illustrative. We'll produce a model tuned to your prompt lengths and qps.
[04:18] Maya: That seems promising. Remember we have HIPAA-like constraints — logs must be redacted, and audit logs retained for 7 years. Is that supported?
[04:29] Grace: We support audit logs and long-term retention as an add-on. For PHI-like data we recommend private deployments or dedicated with customer-managed KMS. We'll attach SOC2 + security docs.
[04:42] Diego: One note on benchmarking: to get realistic batching numbers we need a minute-level traffic trace — per-second qps distribution. If you only provide average qps we'll probably overestimate batching gains.
[04:58] Maya: We can pull a 24-hour sample and share.
[05:02] Ethan: For network, we also do TLS mutual auth in front of endpoints and will want peered VPC endpoints. Any blockers?
[05:10] Diego: That's supported — we'll document the VPC peering and private endpoints. For mutual TLS we do support customer-side certs for dedicated/private.
[05:20] Sara: What's the timeline for the POC? You said 6 weeks — can you break that down?
[05:25] Grace: High level: Week 0 (prep) — scoping, confirm promps and infra; Week 1 — benchmark harness and smoke runs; Weeks 2-3 — full benchmark runs and tuning; Week 4 — cost model review; Week 5 — quality evals and regression checks; Week 6 — final report and decision. We can compress if you prioritize.
[05:44] Maya: That works. Budget-wise, we're approved for a $60k POC budget including any dedicated commit. If dedicated exceeds that we'll need an exec sign-off.
[05:55] Grace: We can model both hosted and a small dedicated commit in the cost spreadsheet. Typically we include break-even analysis showing at what monthly token volume dedicated becomes cheaper.
[06:06] Diego: A couple practicals on batching knobs: we expose max_batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, and adaptive batching. For conversaional workloads you might set lower latency MS and rely more on KV cache; for high-throughput background jobs you can raise batch latency to get more packing. We'll recommend initial values in the spreadsheet.
[06:29] Maya: What's adaptive batching?
[06:31] Diego: It's our runtime that dynamically packs requests based on queue depth and latency SLOs to maximize GPU utilization. It's useful when traffic has variable bursts.
[06:40] Ethan: Any special kernels or quantization you'd recommend for our models? We're leaning towards 4-bit quantization for cost.
[06:47] Diego: 4-bit quant is supported for many open models and gives big memory and cost wins. We'll run quality regressions as part of the POC — sometimes small quality hits are acceptable depending on your eval threshold. We'll show PSNR-like metrics or semantic similarity.
[07:03] Sara: What about fallback and graceful degradation — in case capacity is constrained?
[07:07] Grace: Redwood routing supports fallback to smaller model variants, regional fallback, and priority routing for paid tiers. We can configure automatic fallbacks for the POC.
[07:18] Maya: For the benchmark metrics, can you include cost per 1M tokens, cost per session, and cost per API call?
[07:23] Diego: Yes we'll include those. We'll also include tokenization overhead — some of your prompts may tokenise larger than character counts.
[07:32] Grace: Action items recap — we'll send the cost model, Diego will prep the benchmark plan, you (Maya) will share prompt sets and traffic trace, Ethan will confirm infra constraints.
[07:44] Maya: Sounds good. A few small Qs: 1) Do you support bringing your own models? 2) Can you log anonymized tokens for quality evals?
[07:52] Diego: 1) Yes, for dedicated and private we can deploy customer models or open models you choose. 2) We can redact or hash tokens and provide anonymized logs for eval while complying with your retention policies.
[08:04] Ethan: On the SOC2 docs — how soon can we get those?
[08:07] Grace: I'll attach SOC2, encryption, KMS and network docs in the follow-up email; expect within 24-48 hours.
[08:15] Sara: For cost modeling, will the spreadsheet show sensitivity to batch latency and cache hit rate?
[08:20] Grace: Yes — we'll provide sliders/columns for batch latency, avg batch size, cache hit rate, and utilization to show end-to-end cost impact.
[08:29] Maya: Great. Any blockers on your side?
[08:31] Diego: No blockers. We might need a short infra call with Ethan during smoke runs to validate peering and certs.
[08:39] Ethan: Happy to do that.
[08:41] Grace: Okay, any other questions?
[08:42] Maya: One more — for quantized models, what are the typical delta in latency? We've seen sometimes latency increases slightly if kernels aren't optimal.
[08:50] Diego: Good point. Quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput, but kernel support matters. We'll select kernels with fused-int8/4 ops; if a model falls back to less optimized kernels you'll see some perf hits. We'll call these out in the bench report.
[09:05] Sara: Can you include a sample config for low-latency vs high-throughput modes?
[09:09] Diego: Yes we'll include example runtime configs and recommended batch knobs per workload.
[09:15] Grace: Ok let's recap next steps and owners — Grace: send docs and cost sheet; Diego: benchmark plan; Maya/Ethan: provide data and infra constraints. We'll target the benchmark run week of 2025-12-08 and a follow-up to review results on 2025-12-15.
[09:37] Maya: Works for me. Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Grace: Thanks all — we'll follow up.

Notes: Transcript contains some transcription errors (e.g., K-V cache, psnr mentions, some proper nouns). References: "cost model spreadsheet (link)" will be sent in follow up, "SOC2 + security pack (link)" will be attached.
